title: Fibre products of algebraic spaces and pullback of etale coverings
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $F,G,H$ be algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $F\to H$, $G\to H$ be morphisms. The sheaf fibre product $F\times_HG$ is an algebraic space and is a fibre product in the category of algebraic spaces over $S$. If $\{H_i\to H\}_{i\in I}$ is a jointly surjective etale family of algebraic spaces and $G\to H$ is any morphism, then $\{G\times_HH_i\to G\}_{i\in I}$ is again a jointly surjective etale family. Here scheme fibre products are [def-pc-fibre-product], and etale maps of algebraic spaces are representable as in [def-trf-algebraic-space]; in particular $G\times_HH_i$ is a scheme if $G$ is a scheme and $H_i\to H$ is etale. In the joint-surjectivity clause, $|X|$ denotes the set of equivalence classes of maps $\operatorname{Spec}K\to X$, with $K$ a field [def-weil-field]; two maps represent the same point if their pullbacks to some common field extension agree. A family is jointly surjective if the union of its images on these sets is all of the target point set.

proof.text: Put $P(T)=\{(x,y)\in F(T)\times G(T):f(x)=g(y)\text{ in }H(T)\}$, with componentwise restrictions. This is a sheaf: a matching family of pairs glues uniquely in $F$ and $G$; the images of the two glued sections in $H(T)$ agree because their restrictions agree on the covering and $H$ is a sheaf. This uses the sheaf equalizer condition in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and the sheaf part of [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Thus $P$ is the sheaf fibre product.

source.place: Tag 04T9, first paragraph of proof: the sheaf condition, expanded using the sheaf equalizer definition

proof.text: To test the diagonal of $P$, take a scheme $T$ and two sections $(x_1,y_1),(x_2,y_2)\in P(T)$. The equality locus $A=T\times_{(x_1,x_2),F\times F,\Delta_F}F$ is a scheme, and likewise $B=T\times_{(y_1,y_2),G\times G,\Delta_G}G$, by representability of the two diagonals. For every scheme $Z\to T$, a section of $A\times_TB$ is precisely simultaneous equality of the two $F$ sections and the two $G$ sections, hence equality of the two $P$ sections. Consequently $A\times_TB$ represents the pullback of $\Delta_P$ to $T$. This scheme exists by [def-pc-fibre-product], so $\Delta_P$ is representable.

source.place: Tag 04T9, diagonal cartesian square, with representability checked directly on a scheme test

proof.text: Choose the representable surjective etale atlases $U\to F$ and $V\to G$ supplied by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The sheaf $W=U\times_HV$ is a scheme: it is the pullback of $\Delta_H:H\to H\times H$ along the map $U\times_SV\to H\times H$ induced by $U\to H$ and $V\to H$. The source of this test is a scheme by [def-pc-fibre-product], and the diagonal of the algebraic space $H$ is representable. The maps to $F$ and $G$ induce $W\to P$.

source.place: Tag 04T9, last paragraph: the scheme atlas U times_H V

proof.text: For a scheme $T\to P$ with components $x:T\to F$, $y:T\to G$, form the schemes $A=T\times_FU$ and $B=T\times_GV$. Their maps to $T$ are surjective etale by the atlas definition. The pullback $T\times_PW$ is represented by $A\times_TB$: on every test scheme its data are exactly the two lifts of $x,y$, whose images in $H$ already agree. The projection $A\times_TB\to B$ is surjective and etale by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]. Composing with $B\to T$ preserves surjectivity by [lem-trf-surjective-morphism-composition] and etaleness by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](2). Thus $W\to P$ is representable surjective etale. Together with steps 1 and 2 this verifies all three algebraic-space conditions and proves that $P$ is an algebraic space.

source.place: Tag 04T9, last paragraph; the atlas tested on schemes, with scheme permanence from Tags 01S1, 02GO and 02GN

proof.text: For any algebraic space $Q$, a morphism $Q\to P$ sends a section $q$ to a compatible pair of sections in $F$ and $G$. Conversely a pair of natural transformations $Q\to F$, $Q\to G$ whose composites to $H$ agree defines $q\mapsto(a(q),b(q))$ in $P$, naturally in the test scheme. These constructions are inverse. Since morphisms of algebraic spaces are natural transformations [def-trf-algebraic-space], this is exactly the required categorical universal property.

source.place: Tag 02X2, universal property in the full subcategory, written on sections

proof.text: Apply the fibre-product construction just proved to $G\to H$ and $H_i\to H$, so $P_i=G\times_HH_i$ is an algebraic space. For every scheme $T\to G$, the pullback $T\times_GP_i$ is $T\times_HH_i$: both functors consist of a section of $T$ and a compatible section of $H_i$. Since $H_i\to H$ is representable etale in the convention of the statement, this is a scheme etale over $T$. Thus each $P_i\to G$ is representable etale by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. In particular, taking $T=G$ when $G$ is a scheme shows that $P_i$ is a scheme, as required.

source.place: Tag 041F(3), etaleness and scheme special case proved directly by the scheme-test definition

proof.text: It remains to prove joint surjectivity, without invoking the omitted proof of Tag 041F(3). Let $z\in|G|$ be represented by $a:\operatorname{Spec}K\to G$. Joint surjectivity of the given family gives $i$ and a representative $b:\operatorname{Spec}L\to H_i$ whose image in $|H|$ is the image of $z$. By the point equivalence relation stated above, there is a common extension $M$ of $K$ and $L$ on which the two maps to $H$ agree. The pair $(a|_M,b|_M)$ is therefore a section of the sheaf $G\times_HH_i$ over $\operatorname{Spec}M$, and its point maps to $z$ because $a|_M$ is equivalent to $a$. This proves that every point is covered. If $I$ is empty, the hypothesis gives $|H|=\varnothing$ and any point of $G$ would map to a point of $H$, so $|G|=\varnothing$ and the conclusion still holds.

lean.statement: theorem fibreProduct_isAlgebraicSpace {S : Scheme.{u}} (F G H : AlgebraicSpace S) (f : F ⟶ H) (g : G ⟶ H) : IsAlgebraicSpace (Limits.pullback f.hom g.hom) ∧ ∀ (Q : AlgebraicSpace S) (a : Q ⟶ F) (b : Q ⟶ G), a ≫ f = b ≫ g → ∃! l : Q.obj ⟶ Limits.pullback f.hom g.hom, l ≫ Limits.pullback.fst f.hom g.hom = a.hom ∧ l ≫ Limits.pullback.snd f.hom g.hom = b.hom
lean.note: The three declarations jointly render the node: sheaf-pullback closure with the full-subcategory universal property; preservation of representable etaleness and joint surjectivity on point classes; and representability of the fibre product when G is a scheme. The point-image condition is expanded on field-valued representatives after extension, via the new definition node.
